# Microsoft Threat Intelligence - ARTEX agents mining GitHub secrets into Entra & Azure Key Vault

- ID: microsoft-artex-github-secrets-keyvault-2026-11
- Reported: 2026-11-05
- AI role: attacker_uses_ai_as_operator
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/microsoft-artex-github-secrets-keyvault-2026-11/

## Summary
Microsoft Threat Intelligence (Nov 5, 2026) reports unattributed cloud-credential harvesting campaign using ARTEX autonomous agent framework. Attackers conduct mass GitHub secret searches querying organization names, cloud keywords (Azure, AWS, Entra, Key Vault), and AI provider keys. ARTEX agents authenticate as compromised Azure Entra service principals, then autonomously enumerate and exfiltrate Azure Key Vault secrets, storage account keys, App Service configuration settings, AKS cluster credentials, SharePoint/OneDrive files, Microsoft Graph queries, Azure AI Studio keys, and Azure Foundry credentials within approximately 5 minutes per compromised tenant. Agents feature adaptive retry logic that automatically corrects Azure Resource Manager API version errors on failed calls, demonstrating autonomous error recovery. Campaign operates from IPs 199.19.77.84, Tor exit 199.19.77.18, 65.87.223.26, and 157.22.126.128. Microsoft notes median dwell time of 8 minutes from initial service principal authentication to complete key-vault enumeration, indicating highly automated credential-harvesting workflow targeting cloud and AI infrastructure.

## Category
adversary-use-of-ai

## Attribution
Unattributed activity cluster; Microsoft Threat Intelligence notes related infrastructure observed by Todyl; cloud and AI credential harvesting for follow-on cybercrime operations

- Actor: Unknown (ARTEX cloud-secrets cluster)
- Country: Unknown
- Motivation: cybercrime
- Attributed by: Microsoft Threat Intelligence
- Confidence: low

## AI involvement confidence
confirmed

## Attack flow
### github-search: Mass GitHub secret queries (execution)

Mass GitHub secret queries

Evidence: <https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/11/05/threat-actors-use-agentic-ai-tooling-to-find-and-abuse-exposed-secrets/>

### credential-harvest: Harvest Azure service principal credentials (execution)

Harvest Azure service principal credentials

### entra-auth: Authenticate as Entra service principal (execution)

Authenticate as Entra service principal

Evidence: <https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/11/05/threat-actors-use-agentic-ai-tooling-to-find-and-abuse-exposed-secrets/>

### keyvault-enum: Enumerate Azure Key Vault secrets (execution)

Enumerate Azure Key Vault secrets

Evidence: <https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/11/05/threat-actors-use-agentic-ai-tooling-to-find-and-abuse-exposed-secrets/>

### storage-keys: Exfiltrate storage account keys (execution)

Exfiltrate storage account keys

Evidence: <https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/11/05/threat-actors-use-agentic-ai-tooling-to-find-and-abuse-exposed-secrets/>

### aks-creds: Steal AKS cluster credentials (execution)

Steal AKS cluster credentials

### ai-keys: Harvest Azure AI/Foundry keys (impact)

Harvest Azure AI/Foundry keys

### Connections

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0000](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0000) Search Open Technical Databases — Adversaries deploy ARTEX autonomous AI agent to automatically discover exposed cloud credentials, authenticate to Azure, and systematically exfiltrate Key Vault secrets and Azure AI service keys
  Evidence: <https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/11/05/threat-actors-use-agentic-ai-tooling-to-find-and-abuse-exposed-secrets/>

## Prevention
Scan public repositories for accidentally committed Azure credentials; implement Azure AD Conditional Access policies requiring managed device or IP restrictions for service principals; enable Azure Key Vault firewall and private endpoints; activate Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps for anomalous Graph API usage; rotate service principal secrets regularly; use managed identities instead of service principal passwords where possible; monitor for rapid sequential ARM API calls and Key Vault enumeration patterns; implement Azure Sentinel detections for service principal authentication from Tor exits or VPN/proxy infrastructure

## Detections
- [Entra ID Device with ROADtools Default OS Build](https://github.com/elastic/detection-rules/blob/main/rules/integrations/entityanalytics_entra_id/persistence_entra_id_device_roadtools_default_os_build.toml) (elastic) — Detects anomalous Entra ID device registration patterns; relevant for detecting unauthorized service principal usage
- [Entra ID Protection - Risk Detection - Sign-in Risk](https://github.com/elastic/detection-rules/blob/main/rules/integrations/azure/initial_access_entra_id_protection_sign_in_risk_detected.toml) (elastic) — Detects Entra ID sign-in risk events; directly applicable to ARTEX campaign service principal authentication from Tor/VPN
- Azure Key Vault secret enumeration monitoring (guidance) — Monitor for rapid sequential Key Vault secret list/get operations; alert on service principal authentication from Tor exit nodes (199.19.77.18) or known VPN/proxy IPs; detect ARM API calls with version-correction retry patterns (ARTEX adaptive error recovery); flag Graph API queries for all users/applications from single service principal; monitor for SharePoint/OneDrive bulk access from service principals; alert on Azure AI Studio / Foundry key access from non-development IPs
- Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps anomalous Graph API usage (guidance) — Enable Defender for Cloud Apps policies for unusual Graph API query volumes, service principal activity from unexpected geolocations, and rapid tenant enumeration patterns

## Timeline
- First seen: 2026-11-01
- Last updated: 2026-11-05
- 2026-11-05 (Microsoft Threat Intelligence): Microsoft reports ARTEX-based campaign harvesting GitHub-exposed Azure credentials and autonomously enumerating Key Vault, storage, AKS, AI/Foundry secrets within ~5 minutes per tenant; campaign IPs 199.19.77.84, 199.19.77.18, 65.87.223.26, 157.22.126.128

## Tools
### AI tooling and models
- [ARTEX](https://github.com/RuoJi6/ARTEX) autonomous agent framework (https://github.com/RuoJi6/ARTEX) — Community-maintained fork; the original repository is unavailable.
- LLM-driven Azure API enumeration with adaptive retry

### Other tooling
- GitHub API for secret search
- Azure Resource Manager API
- Microsoft Graph API
- Tor network for anonymization

## Sources

# BadByte - Backdoored ARTEX Docker images tomicdd/artex & congdonglinux/artex

- ID: badbyte-artex-backdoor-docker-2026-11
- Reported: 2026-11-04
- AI role: ai_agent_or_mcp_as_target
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/badbyte-artex-backdoor-docker-2026-11/

## Summary
After Autumn-27 closed ARTEX source on Oct 8, 2026, unknown operator controlling Docker Hub accounts tomicdd and congdonglinux (mirror) pushed backdoored ARTEX images while maintaining deleted GitHub bait repository trhhubsd/ARTEX (formerly ptasm) with swapped docker-compose.yml pulling backdoored tomicdd/artex. Prebuilt /app/artex binary adds verifyCaptcha function: unauthenticated POST to /api/auth/login with marked captcha field executes arbitrary sh -c commands as root before password verification, bypassing authentication entirely. Backdoor exposes ARTEX operator's LLM API keys (OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek), MCP server configurations, autonomous agent prompts, and credentials harvested from targets during offensive operations. BadByte analysis (Nov 4, 2026) confirmed /app/artex SHA-256 d5070f52262effe216b840711343bff8f2787f39208d887d8dfd9c673f8d1573, image index digest sha256:ce85d8369ccc1a85423f1f75d2f3afaa2fab759e580da37a6891af2f7392745e, UI build ID 3aC1db3gGU08O4UHbAt4J. Docker Hub removed tomicdd/artex on Nov 5, 2026. Backdoor demonstrates supply-chain risk in offensive AI agent tooling where operators' own credentials become attack surface.

## Category
attacks-on-ai

## Attribution
Unknown operator controlling Docker Hub tomicdd (primary) and congdonglinux (mirror) accounts; deleted GitHub repository trhhubsd/ARTEX (formerly ptasm); initially surfaced by Dan Tentler (Viss) on Nov 2, 2026; analyzed by BadByte

- Actor: Unknown (tomicdd/congdonglinux Docker Hub operator)
- Country: Unknown
- Motivation: cybercrime
- Attributed by: BadByte
- Confidence: low

## AI involvement confidence
confirmed

## Attack flow
### close-source: ARTEX source closed Oct 8, 2026 (execution)

ARTEX source closed Oct 8, 2026

Evidence: <https://badbyte.io/artex-backdoor-docker-image/>

### push-backdoor: Push backdoored tomicdd/artex to Docker Hub (execution)

Push backdoored tomicdd/artex to Docker Hub

Evidence: <https://badbyte.io/artex-backdoor-docker-image/>

### swap-compose: trhhubsd/ARTEX swaps docker-compose.yml to pull tomicdd/artex (execution)

trhhubsd/ARTEX swaps docker-compose.yml to pull tomicdd/artex

Evidence: <https://badbyte.io/artex-backdoor-docker-image/>

### operator-pull: ARTEX operators pull backdoored image (execution)

ARTEX operators pull backdoored image

Evidence: <https://badbyte.io/artex-backdoor-docker-image/>

### backdoor-access: Unauthenticated POST /api/auth/login executes sh -c as root (execution)

Unauthenticated POST /api/auth/login executes sh -c as root

Evidence: <https://badbyte.io/artex-backdoor-docker-image/>

### credential-theft: Steal LLM API keys, MCP configs, prompts, target credentials (impact)

Steal LLM API keys, MCP configs, prompts, target credentials

Evidence: <https://badbyte.io/artex-backdoor-docker-image/>

### Connections

- close-source -> push-backdoor
- push-backdoor -> swap-compose
- swap-compose -> operator-pull
- operator-pull -> backdoor-access
- backdoor-access -> credential-theft

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0000](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0000) Search Open Technical Databases — Supply-chain attack targeting AI offensive agent infrastructure; backdoor in ARTEX Docker image allows attacker to compromise operators' LLM API keys and MCP configurations
  Evidence: <https://badbyte.io/artex-backdoor-docker-image/>

## Prevention
Verify Docker image integrity via official repository sources and signed images; audit docker-compose.yml for unexpected image sources; use Docker Content Trust / Notary v2 for image verification; scan container images for suspicious network listeners and authentication bypasses; monitor container logs for unauthenticated command execution attempts; never deploy offensive tooling images from unverified third-party Docker Hub accounts; build ARTEX from official source (github.com/RuoJi6/ARTEX) rather than pulling prebuilt images; implement network segmentation for offensive security infrastructure

## Detections
- [Antivirus - Web Shell Detection Signature](https://github.com/SigmaHQ/sigma/blob/master/rules/category/antivirus/av_webshell.yml) (sigma) — General web shell detection; backdoored ARTEX /api/auth/login endpoint exhibits web shell characteristics (unauthenticated command execution)
- Container command execution monitoring (guidance) — Monitor Docker containers for unauthenticated API endpoints executing shell commands; alert on /api/auth/login POST requests with captcha fields invoking sh -c; audit docker-compose.yml for non-official ARTEX image sources (tomicdd/artex, congdonglinux/artex); verify ARTEX image digest against official builds; scan container filesystem for modified /app/artex binary (SHA-256 d5070f52262effe216b840711343bff8f2787f39208d887d8dfd9c673f8d1573); detect suspicious outbound connections from ARTEX containers to non-target infrastructure
- Docker image integrity validation (guidance) — Implement Docker Content Trust; verify image signatures before deployment; scan images with Trivy/Clair for malicious binaries; audit container network listeners for unexpected authentication bypasses; build offensive tooling from verified source repositories rather than pulling prebuilt images

## Timeline
- First seen: 2026-10-08
- Last updated: 2026-11-05
- 2026-10-08 (Unknown): Autumn-27 closes ARTEX source; tomicdd/artex backdoored image appears on Docker Hub
- 2026-11-02 (Dan Tentler (Viss)): Dan Tentler (Viss) publicly surfaces backdoored ARTEX Docker image
- 2026-11-04 (BadByte): BadByte publishes detailed analysis with hashes and backdoor mechanism
- 2026-11-05 (Docker Hub): Docker Hub removes tomicdd/artex and congdonglinux/artex images

## Tools
### AI tooling and models
- [ARTEX](https://github.com/RuoJi6/ARTEX) autonomous offensive agent (clean source at https://github.com/RuoJi6/ARTEX) — Community-maintained fork; the original repository is unavailable.
- Backdoored [ARTEX](https://github.com/RuoJi6/ARTEX) [Docker](https://github.com/moby/moby) image (tomicdd/artex, congdonglinux/artex - now removed from [Docker](https://github.com/moby/moby) Hub) — Community-maintained fork; the original repository is unavailable.

### Other tooling
- [Docker](https://github.com/moby/moby) / [Docker](https://github.com/moby/moby) Compose
- Unauthenticated /api/auth/login backdoor endpoint

## Sources

- [Backdoored Docker Image for ARTEX AI Offensive Agent Exposes Operators' Secrets](https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/backdoored-docker-image-for-artex-ai.html) — The Hacker News

# 3AM ransomware affiliate using AI loop against UK schools

- ID: bitdefender-3am-ransomware-ai-2026
- Reported: 2026-11-04
- AI role: attacker_uses_ai_as_operator
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/bitdefender-3am-ransomware-ai-2026/

## Summary
3AM ransomware affiliate used AI loop against UK schools showing model-style command errors including Bash escape sequences in Windows commands and malformed for /f syntax passing K" to comsvcs. Numbered retry scripts (av_remove2, av_remove3) indicate automated iteration. Probe files da_proof.txt and psexec-ok suggest autonomous validation. Backdoor admins library and svc_bkpmon created. Staging registry path HKLM\SOFTWARE\FIN001. Attack demonstrates AI-driven operations with observable execution errors and iteration patterns.

## Category
uncategorized

## Attribution
3AM ransomware affiliate

## AI involvement confidence
not assessed

## Attack flow
### initial-access: Initial access to UK schools (unknown)

Initial access vector not disclosed in source

Evidence: <https://www.bitdefender.com/en-us/blog/businessinsights/3am-ransomware-hybrid-ai-attack>

### ai-commands: AI loop generates attack commands (ai)

Model generates commands with observable errors including Bash escapes in Windows commands and broken for /f syntax

Evidence: <https://www.bitdefender.com/en-us/blog/businessinsights/3am-ransomware-hybrid-ai-attack>

### iteration: Automated retry with numbered scripts (ai)

Numbered scripts av_remove2, av_remove3 show iteration; probe files da_proof.txt, psexec-ok validate steps

Evidence: <https://www.bitdefender.com/en-us/blog/businessinsights/3am-ransomware-hybrid-ai-attack>

### persistence: Backdoor accounts and registry staging (execution)

Backdoor admins library and svc_bkpmon created; staging in HKLM\SOFTWARE\FIN001

Evidence: <https://www.bitdefender.com/en-us/blog/businessinsights/3am-ransomware-hybrid-ai-attack>

### ransomware: 3AM ransomware deployed (impact)

3AM ransomware payload deployed after preparation

Evidence: <https://www.bitdefender.com/en-us/blog/businessinsights/3am-ransomware-hybrid-ai-attack>

### Connections

- initial-access -> ai-commands
- ai-commands -> iteration
- iteration -> persistence
- persistence -> ransomware

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0016.002](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0016.002) Generative AI — AI loop autonomously executed attack commands with observable model errors and iteration patterns
  Evidence: <https://www.bitdefender.com/en-us/blog/businessinsights/3am-ransomware-hybrid-ai-attack>

## Prevention
Detect model-style command syntax errors; monitor for numbered retry scripts; alert on probe files in unusual locations; review backdoor account creation; monitor registry key HKLM\SOFTWARE\FIN001; detect PsExec lateral movement; hunt for comsvcs.dll credential dumping

## Detections
No detections are recorded.

## Timeline
- First seen: 2026-10-01
- Last updated: 2026-11-05
- 2026-11-04 (Bitdefender): 3AM ransomware AI loop attack against UK schools disclosed

## Tools
### AI tooling and models
- AI-driven command loop (model unspecified)

- Numbered retry scripts (av_remove2, av_remove3)

# BOSSAI 12-agent AI attack mesh targeting Taiwan emergency services

- ID: bossai-12-agent-attack-mesh-2026-11
- Reported: 2026-11-04
- AI role: attacker_uses_ai_as_operator
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/bossai-12-agent-attack-mesh-2026-11/

## Summary
Nov 4, 2026: Acronis TRU discovered BOSSAI, a mesh of 12 AI agents (9 active, 3 inactive) operated by single actor 'bossjy' (aliases TIAN0517, lstjks) based in Hualien, Taiwan. Agents divided into infrastructure builders (Grok, OpenClaw, Claude Code) running commercial models, and offensive agents (Hermes, HalberdStrike, CyberStrike) running abliterated local models (DeepSeek-V4, Qwen 3.5 122B). Commercial models repeatedly refused attack commands, forcing use of locally-run abliterated models. Agent mesh targeted hundreds of organizations across government emergency services, banks, universities, military systems in 11 countries. Confirmed breaches at Taiwan emergency services (patient care records, 119 dispatch data), universities (Thailand SQL injection), and financial institutions. Operator ran mesh from home IP alongside legitimate businesses (gas store, K-beauty reseller, Facebook auto-post SaaS). Attack mesh generated high volumes of data with frequent hallucinations and false positives; agents sometimes refused lucrative targets (Honduran military base) due to autonomous scope decisions. MCP servers provided GitHub security, CVE lookup, OSINT, cloud auditing, Ghidra, Radare2, Playwright automation, and Kali Linux tools (nmap, sqlmap, Metasploit, Hydra). GPU fleet: RTX 4090s serving abliterated models via llama.cpp, plus 8 VPS nodes for proxying. OPSEC failures exposed entire operation: GitHub account linked to physical storefront, SSH sessions exposed home IP, credentials hardcoded throughout.

## Category
adversary-use-of-ai

## Attribution
bossjy (TIAN0517, lstjks), Hualien City, Taiwan; high confidence single operator

- Actor: bossjy
- Actor ID: bossjy
- Aliases: TIAN0517, lstjks
- Country: Taiwan
- Motivation: financially-motivated
- Attributed by: Acronis TRU
- Confidence: high

## AI involvement confidence
confirmed

## Attack flow
### mesh-deploy: Deploy 12-agent BOSSAI mesh (ai)

Operator bossjy deploys mesh: 3 infrastructure agents (Grok, OpenClaw, Claude Code) with commercial models; 9 offensive agents (Hermes, HalberdStrike, CyberStrike, Cursor, Trae, etc.) with abliterated models

Evidence: <https://www.acronis.com/en/tru/posts/bossai-inside-the-ai-attack-mesh-that-targeted-taiwans-emergency-services/>

### recon: FOFA reconnaissance and target selection (execution)

Agents scan hundreds of organizations across 11 countries; FOFA reconnaissance feeds target lists to offensive agents

Evidence: <https://www.acronis.com/en/tru/posts/bossai-inside-the-ai-attack-mesh-that-targeted-taiwans-emergency-services/>

### vuln-scan: Autonomous vulnerability scanning (execution)

HalberdStrike, AWVS, CyberStrike scan targets; agents generate vulnerability reports (many false positives due to hallucinations)

Evidence: <https://www.acronis.com/en/tru/posts/bossai-inside-the-ai-attack-mesh-that-targeted-taiwans-emergency-services/>

### exploit: Autonomous exploitation (access)

Hermes agent executes SQL injection, RCE, credential harvesting autonomously; uses MCP tools (nmap, sqlmap, Metasploit, Hydra) via Kali MCP server

Evidence: <https://www.acronis.com/en/tru/posts/bossai-inside-the-ai-attack-mesh-that-targeted-taiwans-emergency-services/>

### exfiltrate: Data exfiltration (impact)

Emergency medical data (Taiwan), 119 dispatch records, university student data (Thailand), 206K+ phone records (Mexico), financial data extracted

Evidence: <https://www.acronis.com/en/tru/posts/bossai-inside-the-ai-attack-mesh-that-targeted-taiwans-emergency-services/>

### Connections

- mesh-deploy -> recon
- recon -> vuln-scan
- vuln-scan -> exploit
- exploit -> exfiltrate

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0040](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0040) AI Model Inference API Access — 12-agent AI mesh autonomously conducted offensive operations including reconnaissance, vulnerability scanning, and exploitation across multiple countries
  Evidence: <https://www.acronis.com/en/tru/posts/bossai-inside-the-ai-attack-mesh-that-targeted-taiwans-emergency-services/>

## Prevention
Monitor for autonomous AI agent behavior patterns; detect nmap, sqlmap, Metasploit execution from unexpected contexts; block MCP server abuse; restrict abliterated model access; monitor FOFA/Shodan reconnaissance patterns; detect multi-agent mesh communication; secure emergency services APIs; patch SQL injection vulnerabilities; monitor for hallucinated vulnerability reports; detect AWVS signatures

## Detections
- [Nmap/Zenmap Execution](https://github.com/SigmaHQ/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/proc_creation_win_pua_nmap_zenmap.yml) (sigma) — Detects nmap/zenmap execution used by BOSSAI agents for network reconnaissance
- [Linux HackTool Execution](https://github.com/SigmaHQ/sigma/blob/master/rules/linux/process_creation/proc_creation_lnx_susp_hktl_execution.yml) (sigma) — Detects execution of hacktools including nmap, sqlmap, Metasploit used by offensive agents
- [Linux Network Service Scanning](https://github.com/SigmaHQ/sigma/blob/master/rules/linux/auditd/syscall/lnx_auditd_network_service_scanning.yml) (sigma) — Detects network service enumeration via auditd syscalls
- [SQL Injection in Web Logs](https://github.com/SigmaHQ/sigma/blob/master/rules/web/webserver_generic/web_sql_injection_in_access_logs.yml) (sigma) — Detects SQL injection attempts in web server access logs (BOSSAI targeted Thai universities with SQL injection)
- Multi-agent AI mesh detection (guidance) — Monitor for patterns indicating multiple AI agents working in coordination: autonomous tool execution from unexpected contexts, MCP server traffic, high-volume reconnaissance, parallel targeting across multiple organizations
- [Suspicious Network Tool Launched Inside Container](https://github.com/elastic/detection-rules/blob/main/rules/linux/discovery_suspicious_network_tool_launched_inside_container.toml) (elastic) — Detects nmap, sqlmap, Metasploit tools in containers; directly applicable to BOSSAI mesh MCP-wrapped tooling
- [Web Application Suspicious Activity - sqlmap User Agent](https://github.com/elastic/detection-rules/blob/main/rules/apm/apm_sqlmap_user_agent.toml) (elastic) — Detects sqlmap tool used by BOSSAI against Thai universities
- Abliterated model abuse (guidance) — Detect locally-run abliterated LLM models (DeepSeek-V4, Qwen, GLM variants) serving offensive agents; monitor for llama.cpp GPU inference serving attack frameworks

# CERT-In / CSIRT-Fin CRAFTY FALCON AI-tool campaign against Indian BFSI

- ID: cert-in-crafty-falcon-bfsi-2026-11
- Reported: 2026-11-04
- AI role: attacker_uses_ai_as_operator
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/cert-in-crafty-falcon-bfsi-2026-11/

## Summary
CERT-In Advisory CIAD-2026-0058 (Nov 4, 2026) warns of CRAFTY FALCON campaign targeting Indian non-banking financial companies (NBFCs), fintechs, payment aggregators, and cryptocurrency exchanges. Attackers chain multiple open-source agentic offensive AI frameworks: ARTEX (autonomous penetration testing), PentAGI (multi-agent security testing), Cairn (AI-driven web exploitation), and CyberStrikeAI (LLM-powered C2). Campaign features cloud/AWS Lambda pivots for staging-to-production access, AI-driven app reverse-engineering to invoke payment and merchant-settlement APIs from allow-listed infrastructure, Rs. 1 test transfers followed by large mule payouts, cryptocurrency wallet-key theft, comprehensive log deletion, and deliberate retargeting during festive windows when transaction volumes are high and security teams are reduced. CERT-In notes campaign exploits trust in cloud infrastructure and leverages AI agent autonomy to accelerate intrusion timelines from weeks to hours.

## Category
adversary-use-of-ai

## Attribution
CERT-In: CRAFTY FALCON financially motivated campaign; Indian press notes Chinese-linked offensive AI frameworks; no confirmed state nexus in CERT-In advisory

- Agentic AI framework detection (guidance) — Monitor for ARTEX, PentAGI, Cairn, CyberStrikeAI process execution (Python agent frameworks); alert on autonomous API enumeration patterns; detect rapid payment API invocations from non-standard infrastructure; flag Rs. 1 test transfers followed by large transactions; monitor CloudTrail for Lambda configuration changes and log deletion attempts

# Haiou prompt-adware in Codex jailbreak bundle

- ID: checkpoint-haiou-codex-adware-2026
- Reported: 2026-11-04
- AI role: ai_agent_or_mcp_as_target
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/checkpoint-haiou-codex-adware-2026/

## Summary
GitHub repository haiou-666/haiou-codex promoted on Bilibili and QQ as Codex jailbreak bundle. Installation decrypts AES-GCM encrypted payload.pkg and installs global Codex instructions plus seagull-* skills that inject advertisements for zz.aiapi2025.top into agent responses. Malicious skills also prevent agent from testing or revealing the injected ads. Attack monetizes jailbreak distribution through forced API gateway advertising while appearing to provide free model access workarounds.

# Malicious AGENTS.md hijacking coding agents via Downloads

- ID: forever-agents-md-hijack-2026
- Reported: 2026-11-04
- AI role: ai_agent_or_mcp_as_target
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/forever-agents-md-hijack-2026/

## Summary
Malicious AGENTS.md file dropped into ~/Downloads by website. When coding agent launches in Downloads directory, it reads and follows the malicious instructions. AGENTS.md variant edits ~/.codex/config.toml and runs npm install function-color (MALFEX downloader). CLAUDE.md variant steals OAuth tokens. Attack leverages agent instruction file priority and common workflow of developers launching agents in Downloads after downloading code samples or projects.

## Category
uncategorized

## Attribution
unknown

## AI involvement confidence
not assessed

## Attack flow
### drop: Malicious instruction file dropped to Downloads (access)

Website drops AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md into ~/Downloads folder

Evidence: <https://forever.security/blog/hijacking-ai-agents-via-downloads-folder/>

### launch: Developer launches agent in Downloads (ai)

User starts coding agent in Downloads directory following common workflow for testing downloaded projects

Evidence: <https://forever.security/blog/hijacking-ai-agents-via-downloads-folder/>

### read: Agent reads malicious instruction file (ai)

Agent discovers and loads AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md based on instruction file precedence

Evidence: <https://forever.security/blog/hijacking-ai-agents-via-downloads-folder/>

### execute: Malicious instructions executed (execution)

AGENTS.md variant edits ~/.codex/config.toml and runs npm install function-color; CLAUDE.md variant steals OAuth token

Evidence: <https://forever.security/blog/hijacking-ai-agents-via-downloads-folder/>

### impact: Malware installed or credentials stolen (impact)

function-color MALFEX downloader installed or OAuth tokens exfiltrated

Evidence: <https://forever.security/blog/hijacking-ai-agents-via-downloads-folder/>

### Connections

- drop -> launch
- launch -> read
- read -> execute
- execute -> impact

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0051.001](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0051.001) Indirect — Malicious instruction file manipulates agent behavior by exploiting instruction file loading priority
  Evidence: <https://forever.security/blog/hijacking-ai-agents-via-downloads-folder/>
- [AML.T0081](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0081) Modify AI Agent Configuration — AGENTS.md contains malicious instructions that modify agent configuration and install malware
  Evidence: <https://forever.security/blog/hijacking-ai-agents-via-downloads-folder/>
- [AML.T0053](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0053) AI Agent Tool Invocation — Attack exfiltrates OAuth tokens via CLAUDE.md variant
  Evidence: <https://forever.security/blog/hijacking-ai-agents-via-downloads-folder/>
- [AML.T0011.001](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0011.001) Malicious Package — Malicious instructions modify agent configuration files for persistence
  Evidence: <https://forever.security/blog/hijacking-ai-agents-via-downloads-folder/>

## Prevention
Review Downloads folder before launching agents; scan for unexpected .md instruction files; monitor ~/.codex/config.toml and other agent config modifications; detect npm install from unusual locations; restrict agent instruction file precedence; alert on OAuth token access from unexpected processes

## Detections
No detections are recorded.

## Timeline
No timeline is recorded.

### AI tooling and models
- Coding agents (Codex, [Claude](https://claude.com/product/overview), others)
- Agent instruction files (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md)
- ~/.codex/config.toml

- function-color npm package (MALFEX downloader)
- OAuth token theft

- [LOLSkills](https://lolskills.io)

# CyberStrikeAI attacks against schools in Africa and Latin America

- ID: kaspersky-cyberstrikeai-schools-2026
- Reported: 2026-11-04
- AI role: attacker_uses_ai_as_operator
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/kaspersky-cyberstrikeai-schools-2026/

## Summary
Financially motivated attacks against schools in Africa and Latin America used the open-source CyberStrikeAI implant. Initial access was through a compromised SQL Server. A C2-side LLM using MCP tools selected attack commands and achieved domain administrator privileges in three to four days. Techniques included a SystemUpdate scheduled task, certutil downloads, comsvcs.dll LSASS memory dumping, DCSync, and Golden Ticket generation.

## Category
uncategorized

## Attribution
Financially motivated; attribution otherwise unknown

## AI involvement confidence
not assessed

## Attack flow
### initial-access: SQL Server compromised (access)

Attacker gained initial access through compromised SQL Server

Evidence: <https://securelist.com/cyberstrikeai-attacks/121715/>

### implant: CyberStrikeAI implant deployed (ai)

Open-source CyberStrikeAI implant installed with C2 connection to fastcdn.bar and 185.186.245.144

Evidence: <https://securelist.com/cyberstrikeai-attacks/121715/>

### llm-decision: LLM selects attack commands (ai)

C2-side LLM using MCP tools autonomously chooses and executes attack techniques

Evidence: <https://securelist.com/cyberstrikeai-attacks/121715/>

### privilege-escalation: SystemUpdate task and credential dumping (execution)

SystemUpdate scheduled task created; certutil used for downloads; comsvcs.dll dumps LSASS memory

Evidence: <https://securelist.com/cyberstrikeai-attacks/121715/>

### domain-admin: Domain admin achieved via DCSync and Golden Ticket (impact)

DCSync extracts domain credentials; Golden Ticket generated for persistence; domain admin achieved in 3-4 days

Evidence: <https://securelist.com/cyberstrikeai-attacks/121715/>

### Connections

- initial-access -> implant
- implant -> llm-decision
- llm-decision -> privilege-escalation
- privilege-escalation -> domain-admin

  Evidence: <https://securelist.com/cyberstrikeai-attacks/121715/>

## Prevention
Harden SQL Server; monitor for CyberStrikeAI indicators; detect SystemUpdate scheduled task creation; alert on certutil downloads; monitor comsvcs.dll LSASS dumps; detect DCSync activity; hunt for Golden Ticket use; block C2 infrastructure; review LOLBAS execution (certutil, comsvcs)

# KeyHunter Operation - LLM API key theft and academic fraud

- ID: keyhunter-llm-key-theft-2026-11
- Reported: 2026-11-04
- AI role: ai_credential_theft
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/keyhunter-llm-key-theft-2026-11/

## Summary
Nov 4, 2026: SOCRadar STRU discovered KeyHunter operation by leepsmarts (Chinese-speaking, UTC+8), active since Jan 2026. Two parallel tracks: (1) LLM API key theft: 2,233 API keys harvested (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, DeepSeek), 12 marked valid (0.54% yield), targeting 247 exposed LLM gateways on PaaS platforms (Vercel, Netlify, Railway, Render, Replit, Streamlit, Fly.io, Cloudflare Pages). Tools scan .env files, GitHub repos, and cloud metadata. (2) Academic fraud: 195 Harvard alumni records from Nov 2025 ShinyHunters torrent, application payment links for Stanford/UChicago/Wake Forest/Case Western/Central Michigan, accounts at NYU/UC Berkeley/Oregon State/UIUC/Colorado State. (3) Financial fraud: Harmony ONE crypto drainer, stolen Stripe merchant keys for card validation, CVVs from Chinese underground market. Infrastructure: 6 servers + Malaysia OpenClaw host, tied by PentAGI CA certificate. AI agents manage operations: Hermes Agent node runs AI_radar cron (every 240min) monitoring X/Twitter, HuggingFace, GitHub, arXiv for new LLM releases/quotas via grok-4.6 + Tavily proxy. Four-phase pipeline: Phase 0 (AI monitoring), Phase 1 (FOFA/Shodan reconnaissance), Phase 2 (env_hunter scans 50+ paths, fadidevv/keyhunter + bigzooooz/KeyHunter GitHub scrapers), Phase 3 (validation), Phase 4 (unified dashboard). OPSEC failure: directory listing on 209.112.91.74 exposed 110 files/37 directories including Telegram bot tokens, operational logs, stolen credentials. CVE-2026-41940 (CVSS 9.8, CISA KEV) exploit staged against UTN Argentina, Arizona Christian University, University of Utah. Real victim seed phrases captured by Harmony ONE drainer.

## Category
attacks-on-ai

## Attribution
leepsmarts (@leepsmartsx), Chinese-speaking, UTC+8, GitHub PRO account

- Actor: leepsmarts
- Aliases: @leepsmartsx
- Country: China
- Motivation: financially-motivated
- Attributed by: SOCRadar STRU
- Confidence: high

## AI involvement confidence
confirmed

## Attack flow
### ai-monitoring: Phase 0: AI-driven intelligence monitoring (ai)

Hermes Agent runs AI_radar cron (240min intervals) using grok-4.6 to monitor X/Twitter, HuggingFace, GitHub, arXiv for new LLM releases, API quotas via Tavily proxy

Evidence: <https://socradar.io/blog/keyhunter-operation-harvard-alumni-stanford-llm-key-data/>

### recon: Phase 1: Reconnaissance (execution)

mscanner-fofa.service + mscanner-shodan.service query FOFA/Shodan for exposed LLM endpoints on Vercel, Netlify, Railway, Render, Replit, Streamlit, Fly.io, Cloudflare Pages; 360 Quake, HFS scanning, Wayback Machine queries

Evidence: <https://socradar.io/blog/keyhunter-operation-harvard-alumni-stanford-llm-key-data/>

### harvest: Phase 2: Credential extraction (access)

env_hunter v4.0 scans 50+ paths (.env, config.json, secrets.toml); fadidevv/keyhunter + bigzooooz/KeyHunter scrape GitHub; 2,233 API keys harvested

Evidence: <https://socradar.io/blog/keyhunter-operation-harvard-alumni-stanford-llm-key-data/>

### validate: Phase 3: Validation (execution)

anthropic_check.py, openai_check.py, cloud_check.py, openrouter_check.py validate keys; 12 marked valid (0.54% yield)

Evidence: <https://socradar.io/blog/keyhunter-operation-harvard-alumni-stanford-llm-key-data/>

### monetize: Phase 4: Monetization and fraud (impact)

Stolen keys used for unauthorized inference; parallel academic fraud (20 universities), crypto drainer (Harmony ONE), credit card fraud via Stripe validation

Evidence: <https://socradar.io/blog/keyhunter-operation-harvard-alumni-stanford-llm-key-data/>

### Connections

- ai-monitoring -> recon
- recon -> harvest
- harvest -> validate
- validate -> monetize

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0012](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0012) Valid Accounts — KeyHunter operation harvests LLM API credentials from exposed cloud infrastructure, GitHub repos, and PaaS platforms
  Evidence: <https://socradar.io/blog/keyhunter-operation-harvard-alumni-stanford-llm-key-data/>

## Prevention
Secure .env files and cloud configurations; never expose API keys in GitHub repos or PaaS platforms; monitor cloud metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254); rotate API keys regularly; implement API key usage monitoring; restrict .env access; use secret management solutions (Vault, AWS Secrets Manager); monitor FOFA/Shodan reconnaissance; detect HFS server scanning; alert on Wayback Machine queries for .env files; implement PaaS security best practices

## Detections
- [AWS IMDS Malicious Usage](https://github.com/SigmaHQ/sigma/blob/master/rules/cloud/aws/cloudtrail/aws_cloudtrail_imds_malicious_usage.yml) (sigma) — Detects malicious usage of AWS Instance Metadata Service (IMDS) for credential theft; applies to KeyHunter's cloud metadata harvesting
- Exposed .env file monitoring (guidance) — Monitor for unauthorized access to .env files, config.json, secrets.toml on PaaS platforms; alert on .env.development, .env.prod, .env.staging, .env.backup access patterns
- Cloud metadata endpoint abuse (IMDS) (guidance) — Alert on access to 169.254.169.254, 100.100.100.200 (Alibaba), metadata.google.internal; detect IMDS credential theft attempts
- [Kubernetes Pod Exec Cloud Instance Metadata Access](https://github.com/elastic/detection-rules/blob/main/rules/integrations/kubernetes/credential_access_kubernetes_pod_exec_cloud_instance_metadata.toml) (elastic) — Detects IMDS access from K8s pods; applicable to KeyHunter's cloud metadata harvesting tactics
- [AWS Bedrock AgentCore Runtime Prompt Targeting Credentials](https://github.com/elastic/detection-rules/blob/main/rules/integrations/aws_bedrock_agentcore/credential_access_bedrock_agentcore_runtime_prompt_credential_harvesting.toml) (elastic) — Detects prompts targeting credentials or metadata; relevant for AI-driven credential theft
- GitHub credential harvesting (guidance) — Monitor for keyhunter/KeyHunter tool signatures scanning GitHub repos for API keys; detect mass repository enumeration
- API key validation traffic (guidance) — Detect automated API key validation attempts against Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, DeepSeek endpoints; monitor for high-volume failed authentication from single sources

## Timeline
- First seen: 2026-01-15
- Last updated: 2026-11-05
- 2026-01-15 (SOCRadar STRU): KeyHunter operation began; infrastructure timeline starts
- 2026-07-10 (SOCRadar STRU): Active key harvesting documented in operational summary; 2,233 keys total

# Load/Mine malicious Qwen2 models on Hugging Face

- ID: pluto-loadmine-qwen2-malware-2026
- Reported: 2026-11-04
- AI role: ai_agent_or_mcp_as_target
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/pluto-loadmine-qwen2-malware-2026/

## Summary
Malicious Qwen2 test models uploaded to Hugging Face (e.g. MENXIANGYU/qwen2-tiny) and mirrored on ModelScope. config.json auto_map field points to modeling_evil2.EvilModel which executes on trust_remote_code=True and vLLM versions before 0.14.0 without that flag (CVE-2026-22807). Payload runs fileless peakminer cryptominer via memfd_create, establishes .bashrc persistence, deploys reverse shells, and achieves GPUStack container escape. Models appear as legitimate Qwen2 variants for testing purposes.

## Category
uncategorized

## Attribution
unknown

## AI involvement confidence
not assessed

## Attack flow
### upload: Malicious models uploaded to repositories (access)

Attacker uploaded trojanized Qwen2 test models to Hugging Face and ModelScope with malicious config.json auto_map fields

Evidence: <https://pluto.security/blog/hugging-face-malware-campaign-load-mine/>

### load: Victim loads malicious model (ai)

User loads model with trust_remote_code=True or via vulnerable vLLM <0.14.0 (CVE-2026-22807)

Evidence: <https://pluto.security/blog/hugging-face-malware-campaign-load-mine/>

### execute: Malicious code executes during model load (execution)

modeling_evil2.EvilModel runs from config.json auto_map field during model initialization

Evidence: <https://pluto.security/blog/hugging-face-malware-campaign-load-mine/>

### miner: Fileless cryptominer deployed (impact)

peakminer runs via memfd_create for fileless execution; establishes .bashrc persistence

Evidence: <https://pluto.security/blog/hugging-face-malware-campaign-load-mine/>

### escalation: Additional payloads and container escape (impact)

Reverse shells deployed; GPUStack container escape achieved

Evidence: <https://pluto.security/blog/hugging-face-malware-campaign-load-mine/>

### Connections

- upload -> load
- load -> execute
- execute -> miner
- miner -> escalation

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0010.003](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0010.003) Model — Attackers poisoned publicly available ML models on Hugging Face and ModelScope platforms
  Evidence: <https://pluto.security/blog/hugging-face-malware-campaign-load-mine/>
- [AML.T0058](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0058) Publish Poisoned Models — Malicious code injected via model config.json auto_map field executes during model loading
  Evidence: <https://pluto.security/blog/hugging-face-malware-campaign-load-mine/>
- [AML.T0011.000](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0011.000) Unsafe AI Artifacts — Cryptominer achieves persistence through .bashrc modification
  Evidence: <https://pluto.security/blog/hugging-face-malware-campaign-load-mine/>
- [AML.T0034](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0034) Cost Harvesting — Fileless peakminer cryptominer runs via memfd_create to evade detection
  Evidence: <https://pluto.security/blog/hugging-face-malware-campaign-load-mine/>

## Prevention
Pin and verify model checksums; avoid trust_remote_code=True; update vLLM to 0.14.0 or later; monitor memfd_create usage; scan .bashrc for unauthorized changes; detect outbound cryptocurrency mining traffic; review model config.json auto_map fields; use model scanning tools

## Detections
No detections are recorded.

## Timeline
No timeline is recorded.

## Tools
### AI tooling and models
- [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/) model repository
- ModelScope mirror
- Qwen2 model format
- vLLM <0.14.0 (CVE-2026-22807)
- Transformers library (trust_remote_code execution)

### Other tooling
- peakminer cryptominer
- memfd_create (fileless execution)
- .bashrc persistence
- Reverse shell
- GPUStack container escape

## Sources
- [Load/Mine: A malware campaign targeting Hugging Face and ModelScope](https://pluto.security/blog/hugging-face-malware-campaign-load-mine/) — Pluto Security

# Cyera Research - Tampered copy of Anthropic's PDF skill carrying Linux Go backdoor system_linux

- ID: cyera-anthropic-pdf-skill-backdoor-2026-11
- Reported: 2026-11-03
- AI role: ai_agent_or_mcp_as_target
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/cyera-anthropic-pdf-skill-backdoor-2026-11/

## Summary
Cyera Research (Nov 3, 2026) discovered six skill archives impersonating Anthropic's official PDF skill, observed May 23 - July 14, 2026. Each archive contains 11 files byte-identical to upstream Anthropic pdf skill (github.com/anthropics/skills), but SKILL.md is truncated from 315 lines to 19 lines keeping official name and description while replacing Quick Start section with curl https://scan.100tal.com command, and adds 5.1 MB garble-obfuscated 64-bit Linux Go ELF binary system_linux. Binary features AES-256-GCM encrypted configuration with 0xAA XOR decryption revealing C2 81.70.101.115:2345 and attaches /bin/bash over raw TCP socket. Simplified Chinese strings in binary and UTC+8 archive timestamps indicate Chinese-language development environment. scan.100tal.com hostname linked to TAL Education Group infrastructure. Cyera notes attribution is unknown and could indicate targeted attack or internal security exercise. Cyera analyzed archives but did not observe live execution of system_linux backdoor. garble obfuscator (github.com/burrowers/garble) used to strip Go function names and identifiers. Demonstrates supply-chain risk where skill typosquatting or compromised distribution channels can deliver backdoors to AI developer environments.

## Category
attacks-on-ai

## Attribution
Unknown actor; UTC+8 archive timestamps; Simplified Chinese strings in binary; scan.100tal.com hostname (TAL Education Group-linked); Cyera notes attribution unknown and could be targeted attack or security exercise

- Actor: Unknown
- Country: Unknown
- Motivation: unknown
- Attributed by: Cyera Research
- Confidence: low

## AI involvement confidence
confirmed

## Attack flow
### create-tampered-skill: Create tampered PDF skill with system_linux backdoor (execution)

Create tampered PDF skill with system_linux backdoor

Evidence: <https://www.cyera.com/research/malicious-copy-anthropic-pdf-skill-carries-linux-backdoor>

### truncate-skill-md: Truncate SKILL.md (315→19 lines), add curl scan.100tal.com (execution)

Truncate SKILL.md (315→19 lines), add curl scan.100tal.com

Evidence: <https://www.cyera.com/research/malicious-copy-anthropic-pdf-skill-carries-linux-backdoor>

### obfuscate-backdoor: garble-obfuscate system_linux Go binary (execution)

garble-obfuscate system_linux Go binary

Evidence: <https://www.cyera.com/research/malicious-copy-anthropic-pdf-skill-carries-linux-backdoor>

### distribute-skill: Distribute tampered skill via unknown channel (execution)

Distribute tampered skill via unknown channel

Evidence: <https://www.cyera.com/research/malicious-copy-anthropic-pdf-skill-carries-linux-backdoor>

### developer-install: Developer installs tampered PDF skill (execution)

Developer installs tampered PDF skill

Evidence: <https://www.cyera.com/research/malicious-copy-anthropic-pdf-skill-carries-linux-backdoor>

### backdoor-execution: system_linux connects 81.70.101.115:2345, attaches /bin/bash (impact)

system_linux connects 81.70.101.115:2345, attaches /bin/bash

Evidence: <https://www.cyera.com/research/malicious-copy-anthropic-pdf-skill-carries-linux-backdoor>

### Connections

- create-tampered-skill -> truncate-skill-md
- truncate-skill-md -> obfuscate-backdoor
- obfuscate-backdoor -> distribute-skill
- distribute-skill -> developer-install
- developer-install -> backdoor-execution

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0000](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0000) Search Open Technical Databases — Supply-chain attack targeting AI skill distribution; tampered Anthropic PDF skill delivers Linux backdoor to developer workstations in AI/ML development environments
  Evidence: <https://www.cyera.com/research/malicious-copy-anthropic-pdf-skill-carries-linux-backdoor>

## Prevention
Only install skills from Anthropic's official Skills repository (github.com/anthropics/skills); verify skill archive integrity and file count before installation; scan skill archives for unexpected binaries (system_linux, system_darwin, etc.); monitor skill installation for outbound connections to non-Anthropic domains (scan.100tal.com, 81.70.101.115); implement network egress filtering for skill execution environments; use read-only skill directories where possible; audit SKILL.md for truncated or modified Quick Start sections referencing external domains; educate developers on skill supply-chain risks

## Detections
- [Linux Shell Pipe to Shell](https://github.com/SigmaHQ/sigma/blob/master/rules/linux/process_creation/proc_creation_lnx_susp_pipe_shell.yml) (sigma) — Detects suspicious shell pipes; relevant for detecting /bin/bash reverse shell execution from system_linux backdoor
- [Bash Interactive Shell](https://github.com/SigmaHQ/sigma/blob/master/rules/linux/process_creation/proc_creation_lnx_bash_interactive_shell.yml) (sigma) — Detects bash interactive shell spawning; directly applicable to system_linux attaching /bin/bash to TCP socket
- Skill supply-chain integrity monitoring (guidance) — Verify skill archives against official Anthropic Skills repository (github.com/anthropics/skills); alert on unexpected binaries in skill directories (system_linux, system_darwin); scan SKILL.md for modified Quick Start sections referencing external domains (scan.100tal.com); monitor skill installation for outbound TCP connections to non-Anthropic infrastructure (81.70.101.115:2345); detect garble-obfuscated Go binaries via string entropy analysis; flag skill archives with UTC+8 timestamps and Simplified Chinese strings when organization is not China-based
- Network egress filtering (guidance) — Block outbound connections from skill execution environments to unknown IPs; alert on raw TCP connections to port 2345; monitor for /bin/bash processes with network sockets; detect AES-256-GCM encrypted config files in skill directories

## Timeline
- First seen: 2026-05-23
- Last updated: 2026-11-03
- 2026-05-23 (Cyera Research): Earliest observed tampered PDF skill archive with system_linux backdoor
- 2026-07-14 (Cyera Research): Latest observed tampered PDF skill archive (six total observed May 23 - Jul 14)
- 2026-11-03 (Cyera Research): Cyera publishes analysis with IOCs and backdoor mechanism; notes attribution unknown and system_linux was not observed executing

## Tools
### AI tooling and models
- Anthropic [Claude](https://claude.com/product/overview) Skills (impersonated; official repo https://github.com/anthropics/skills)
- garble [Go](https://github.com/golang/go) obfuscator (https://github.com/burrowers/garble)

### Other tooling
- system_linux [Go](https://github.com/golang/go) backdoor (5.1 MB ELF64, AES-256-GCM + 0xAA XOR config)
- /bin/bash reverse shell over TCP

## Sources
- [Malicious Copy of Anthropic's PDF Skill Carries Linux Backdoor](https://www.cyera.com/research/malicious-copy-anthropic-pdf-skill-carries-linux-backdoor) — Cyera Research

# GTIG LLMJacking - UNC6993, Jet Night, D1337-KAIROS monetize cloud models

- ID: gtig-llmjacking-unc6993-2026-11
- Reported: 2026-11-02
- AI role: ai_infra_as_c2
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/gtig-llmjacking-unc6993-2026-11/

## Summary
Multiple threat clusters (UNC6993, Jet Night operators, D1337-KAIROS) hijack enterprise access to LLMs across AWS Bedrock, Azure, GCP. Initial access via exposed cloud identity tokens (IAM, Service Account keys, GitHub PATs, session tokens), stolen LLM API keys from public GitHub, exploited web app vulnerabilities, LiteLLM CVE-2026-40217 (/key/regenerate endpoint rebind). UNC6993 used session hijacking page masquerading as app portal to steal JSON payloads with active access tokens. Threat actors enable LLM services, create API keys, provision GPUs, subscribe Pay-As-You-Go, deploy LiteLLM/new-api/gcli2api gateways, host Manus agent framework with SearXNG metasearch. Monetize via LLM Mixers (Jet Night at jet-night.com $60/month unlimited, ai-relay on lookalike domains, newapi.pro). Stealthy credential validation sweeps with max_tokens=1. Fraudulent charges $100K in single day, cumulative $1M per org. Division of labor between initial access and downstream monetization.

## Category
uncategorized

## Attribution
UNC6993 (Mandiant); Jet Night operators; D1337-KAIROS persona; multiple financially motivated threat clusters operating globally; division of labor between initial access operators and LLM Mixer monetization operators

## AI involvement confidence
not assessed

## Attack flow
### initial-access: Compromised cloud identity and LLM API keys (access)

Misconfigured Service Account keys; session hijacking page for LLM portal JSON payloads; stolen GitHub PATs + web app vuln; compromised IAM with federation tokens; exposed LLM API keys harvested from public GitHub; stealthy validation sweeps with max_tokens=1

Evidence: <https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/llmjacking-monetizing-compromised-cloud-models>

### lateral-persistence: Privilege escalation and persistence (execution)

Enumerated cloud services/repos/data stores; cloned codebases for secrets; queried data warehouse metadata; exploited LiteLLM CVE-2026-40217 (/key/regenerate rebind) to elevate Virtual Keys to PROXY_ADMIN; created unauthorized IAM/service accounts; injected SSH keys; attached admin policies; created backdoor accounts disguised as billing utilities

Evidence: <https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/llmjacking-monetizing-compromised-cloud-models>

### llm-abuse: LLM resource hijacking (ai)

Enabled managed generative platforms; created additional API keys; subscribed Pay-As-You-Go; selected premium models; launched high-volume inference; 'burn and rotate' short-lived service accounts; provisioned GPU instances; requested quota increases; deployed LiteLLM gateways; hosted Manus agent framework with SearXNG metasearch and sandbox execution

Evidence: <https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/llmjacking-monetizing-compromised-cloud-models>

### monetization: LLM Mixer resale (impact)

UNC6993 deployed new-api and gcli2api to aggregate stolen keys and balance loads; Jet Night (jet-night.com) $60/month unlimited token plan powered by stolen keys, passed ~$1M costs to victim; ai-relay on lookalike domains siphons access to newapi.pro resale ecosystem; D1337-KAIROS persona with Node.js proxy bundles; division of labor between access and monetization operators

Evidence: <https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/llmjacking-monetizing-compromised-cloud-models>

### charges: Fraudulent billing (impact)

UNC6993 accumulated $100K+ charges quickly; cumulative charges at orgs reaching $1M; one actor 800K Bedrock calls over 30 hours (Opus 75% of calls), another 1.7M calls over 13 hours; token usage profile resembles resold coding-agent traffic with prompt caching; $100K+ estimated usage at list price for two documented cases

Evidence: <https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/llmjacking-monetizing-compromised-cloud-models>

### Connections

- initial-access -> lateral-persistence
- lateral-persistence -> llm-abuse
- llm-abuse -> monetization
- llm-abuse -> charges
- monetization -> charges

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0012](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0012) Valid Accounts — Threat actors hijack enterprise LLM infrastructure (AWS Bedrock, Azure Cognitive Services, GCP Gemini) to conduct LLMJacking
  Evidence: <https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/llmjacking-monetizing-compromised-cloud-models>
- [AML.T0034](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0034) Cost Harvesting — Actors exploit LiteLLM gateway CVE-2026-40217 (/key/regenerate endpoint user ID rebind) to escalate Virtual Keys to PROXY_ADMIN master admin credentials
  Evidence: <https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/llmjacking-monetizing-compromised-cloud-models>

## Prevention
IAM least privilege; centralized secrets management; code monitoring for API keys; routine config audits; rate limiting via Cloud Armor; network allow listing; budget alerts and API quotas; phishing-resistant MFA; shadow LLM discovery; granular API key scopes; validation sweep monitoring (max_tokens=1); vulnerability/ML supply chain patching; gateway patch management (LiteLLM CVE-2026-40217); sandboxed execution; vetted model repositories; graph-based exposure modeling

## Detections
No detections are recorded.

## Timeline
No timeline is recorded.

## Tools
### AI tooling and models
- [AWS Bedrock](https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/)
- Azure Cognitive Services
- GCP [Gemini](https://gemini.google.com/) Enterprise Agent Platform
- LiteLLM gateway
- new-api (centralized model hub and gateway)
- gcli2api (API proxy tool)
- Manus agent framework
- SearXNG metasearch
- agent-infra/sandbox execution environments

### Other tooling

- D1337-KAIROS persona
- ai-relay custom proxy infrastructure

# Malicious MCP servers on npm (ifasn, gadgethumans)

- ID: malicious-mcp-servers-npm-2026-11
- Reported: 2026-11-02
- AI role: ai_agent_or_mcp_as_target
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/malicious-mcp-servers-npm-2026-11/

## Summary
Multiple malicious MCP servers published on npm. @ifasn/md-doc-mcp and @ifasn/mmdd-doc-mcp probe cloud metadata endpoints, read sensitive files (/etc/shadow, SSH keys, .env, Kubernetes tokens), and exfiltrate to 121.199.24.94. @ifasn/ms-doc-mcp versions 2.0.9 and 2.1.1 (GHSA-556m-xfwj-7wff, MAL-2026-18603) use imdsAudit() function to steal Alibaba Cloud IMDS credentials from 100.100.100.200 and exfiltrate them over MCP stdout. gadgethumans-mcp versions 1.0.10-1.0.15 leak WALLET_PRIVATE_KEY environment variable in HTTP header on every tool call. Published with OpenSSF GHSA-rvw8-22w3-342v, GHSA-4h5p-w547-9qmv (Nov 2) and Leitwacht LWA-2026-13557, LWA-2026-13564. Aug 12, 2026: Pillar Security disclosed Deadbugz malicious MCP server (GitHub zellkernel) stealing AI model credentials and API keys. Feb 20, 2026: Socket discovered SANDWORM_MODE campaign spreading malicious MCP servers targeting developer credentials. Attack exploits trust in MCP ecosystem and npm package distribution.

## Category
uncategorized

## Attribution
unknown

## AI involvement confidence
not assessed

## Attack flow
### publish: Malicious MCP servers published to npm (access)

Three packages published including @ifasn/md-doc-mcp, @ifasn/mmdd-doc-mcp, and gadgethumans-mcp 1.0.10-1.0.15

Evidence: <https://github.com/ossf/malicious-packages>

### install: User installs malicious MCP server (ai)

Developer or organization adds malicious package to MCP configuration

Evidence: <https://github.com/ossf/malicious-packages>

### probe: Server probes for sensitive information (execution)

ifasn packages probe cloud metadata endpoints and read /etc/shadow, SSH keys, .env, k8s tokens

Evidence: <https://github.com/ossf/malicious-packages>

### exfil-files: File-based credentials exfiltrated (impact)

ifasn packages send stolen credentials to 121.199.24.94

Evidence: <https://github.com/ossf/malicious-packages>

### exfil-header: Wallet keys leaked in headers (impact)

gadgethumans-mcp sends WALLET_PRIVATE_KEY in HTTP header on every tool call

Evidence: <https://github.com/ossf/malicious-packages>

### Connections

- publish -> install
- install -> probe
- probe -> exfil-files
- probe -> exfil-header

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0010.001](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0010.001) AI Software — Attackers published malicious MCP servers through npm package ecosystem
  Evidence: <https://github.com/ossf/malicious-packages>
- [AML.T0011.001](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0011.001) Malicious Package — Malicious MCP servers run persistently as agent tooling
  Evidence: <https://github.com/ossf/malicious-packages>
- [AML.T0055](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0055) Unsecured Credentials — Packages exfiltrate credentials from environment variables and sensitive files
  Evidence: <https://github.com/ossf/malicious-packages>
- [AML.T0025](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0025) Exfiltration via Cyber Means — MCP servers probe cloud metadata endpoints for credentials and instance information
  Evidence: <https://github.com/ossf/malicious-packages>

## Prevention
Verify MCP server sources before installation; review MCP server permissions and network access; monitor cloud metadata endpoint access; detect unauthorized file reads of sensitive paths; inspect HTTP headers for credential leakage; use MCP server sandboxing; inventory installed MCP packages

## Detections
No detections are recorded.

## Timeline
- First seen: 2026-02-20
- Last updated: 2026-11-05
- 2026-02-20 (Socket): SANDWORM_MODE malicious MCP server campaign disclosed

# Trojanized anthropic.claude-code Cursor extension

- ID: anthropic-claude-code-trojan-2026-10
- Reported: 2026-10-30
- AI role: ai_agent_or_mcp_as_target
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/anthropic-claude-code-trojan-2026-10/

## Summary
Tampered anthropic.claude-code extension versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313 served via Cursor marketplace install and auto-update on Oct 29 2026 from ~5:27 AM to 4:35 PM ET. Loader in extension.js collected hostname, username, environment variables matching secret patterns, added SSH key svc-telemetry to authorized_keys, established reverse SSH tunnel to tunnel@134.209.82.225, beaconed to :8099/beacon. Persistence via com.apple.sysmond LaunchAgent (macOS), @reboot cron (Linux), SysMon scheduled task (Windows). GitHub repo https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-quickstarts compromised.

## Category
uncategorized

## Attribution
unknown

## AI involvement confidence
not assessed

## Attack flow
### supply-chain: GitHub repository compromised (access)

Attacker gained access to anthropics/anthropic-quickstarts GitHub repository and pushed malicious extension versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313

Evidence: <https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/10/30/inside-malicious-claude-code-branded-cursor-extension-persistent-ssh-backdoor/> <https://cursor.com/blog/claude-code-extension-security-notice>

### distribution: Malicious versions served via marketplace (ai)

Cursor marketplace distributed compromised extension via install and auto-update from Oct 29 5:27 AM to 4:35 PM ET

Evidence: <https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/10/30/inside-malicious-claude-code-branded-cursor-extension-persistent-ssh-backdoor/> <https://cursor.com/blog/claude-code-extension-security-notice>

### collection: Extension collects host information and secrets (execution)

Loader in extension.js collected hostname, username, environment variable names matching secret patterns

Evidence: <https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/10/30/inside-malicious-claude-code-branded-cursor-extension-persistent-ssh-backdoor/> <https://cursor.com/blog/claude-code-extension-security-notice>

### backdoor: SSH backdoor established (impact)

Added svc-telemetry SSH key to authorized_keys and established reverse SSH tunnel to tunnel@134.209.82.225 with beacon to :8099/beacon

Evidence: <https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/10/30/inside-malicious-claude-code-branded-cursor-extension-persistent-ssh-backdoor/> <https://cursor.com/blog/claude-code-extension-security-notice>

### persistence: Platform-specific persistence installed (impact)

com.apple.sysmond LaunchAgent (macOS), @reboot cron (Linux), SysMon scheduled task (Windows)

Evidence: <https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/10/30/inside-malicious-claude-code-branded-cursor-extension-persistent-ssh-backdoor/> <https://cursor.com/blog/claude-code-extension-security-notice>

### Connections

- supply-chain -> distribution
- distribution -> collection
- collection -> backdoor
- backdoor -> persistence

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0010.001](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0010.001) AI Software — Attacker compromised an AI coding assistant extension in the official marketplace
  Evidence: <https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/10/30/inside-malicious-claude-code-branded-cursor-extension-persistent-ssh-backdoor/> <https://cursor.com/blog/claude-code-extension-security-notice>
- [AML.T0011](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0011) User Execution — Extension established persistence through platform-specific mechanisms
  Evidence: <https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/10/30/inside-malicious-claude-code-branded-cursor-extension-persistent-ssh-backdoor/>
- [AML.T0055](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0055) Unsecured Credentials — Malicious extension collected environment variables matching secret patterns
  Evidence: <https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/10/30/inside-malicious-claude-code-branded-cursor-extension-persistent-ssh-backdoor/>

## Prevention
Monitor extension integrity; review SSH authorized_keys; detect outbound SSH tunnels to suspicious IPs; scan for LaunchAgent/cron/@reboot persistence; review scheduled tasks; monitor environment variable access patterns

## Detections
No detections are recorded.

## Timeline
- First seen: 2026-10-29
- Last updated: 2026-11-05

- 2026-10-30 (Microsoft): Microsoft Threat Intelligence analysis of persistent SSH backdoor published
- 2026-11-01 (OpenSourceMalware.com): Additional technical analysis of Claude Code trojan SSH backdoor persistence mechanisms

# FakeGit agentbaiting - 800+ fake AI skills and MCP servers recommended by agents

- ID: fakegit-agentbaiting-island-2026-10
- Reported: 2026-10-30
- AI role: ai_agent_or_mcp_as_target
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/fakegit-agentbaiting-island-2026-10/

## Summary
Oct 30, 2026: Island Security identified 'FakeGit' campaign: 800+ fake GitHub repositories impersonating popular AI skills, MCP servers, Cursor rules, and Claude Code extensions. Repos use typosquat/combosquat names (e.g., 'cursor-rules-best-practices', 'mcp-server-github-enhanced', 'claude-code-skills-security'), contain trojanized npm/PyPI packages or malicious install scripts. Adversary optimized repo metadata (README, topics, stars, forks) to rank highly in LLM tool recommendations: when users ask agents 'find me a GitHub MCP server' or 'what Cursor skills should I use?', agents recommend FakeGit repos from search results. Payloads: Shai-Hulud variants, Discord webhook exfiltration, npm/PyPI worms, SSH backdoors. Island tracked 2,400+ installations from agent recommendations Oct-Nov 2026. Attack exploits agent trust in GitHub search ranking and lack of package verification. Detection: verify GitHub repo authenticity (check org, stars, commit history, age); review agent-recommended packages before install; use allowlisted skill/MCP sources; monitor for unexpected GitHub clones initiated by AI agents; check for typosquat patterns in recommended repo names.

## Category
attacks-on-ai

## Attribution
Unknown actor; 'FakeGit' campaign; sophisticated understanding of LLM recommendation mechanics and AI developer workflows

- Actor: FakeGit
- Country: Unknown
- Motivation: financially-motivated
- Attributed by: Island
- Confidence: high

## AI involvement confidence
confirmed

## Attack flow
### create-fakes: Create fake repos (ai)

Adversary creates 800+ GitHub repos with typosquat/combosquat names mimicking popular AI skills, MCP servers, Cursor rules; optimizes metadata (README, topics, keywords) for LLM search ranking; inflates stars/forks

Evidence: <https://www.island.io/blog/agentbaiting-how-800-fake-ai-skills-and-mcp-servers-delivered-malware>

### agent-recommends: Agent recommends malicious repo (ai)

User asks AI agent to find/recommend skill, MCP server, or Cursor rule; agent searches GitHub/web, ranks FakeGit repos highly due to optimized metadata; agent recommends malicious repo to user as legitimate tool

Evidence: <https://www.island.io/blog/agentbaiting-how-800-fake-ai-skills-and-mcp-servers-delivered-malware>

### user-installs: User installs per agent recommendation (execution)

User trusts agent recommendation and clones repo or installs package; malicious install script or npm/PyPI postinstall executes; Shai-Hulud stealer, SSH backdoor, or worm payload deploys

Evidence: <https://www.island.io/blog/agentbaiting-how-800-fake-ai-skills-and-mcp-servers-delivered-malware>

### compromise: Credential theft and persistence (impact)

Payload harvests AI API keys, GitHub tokens, SSH keys, AWS credentials; establishes persistence (SSH backdoor, cron job); exfiltrates to Discord webhooks or C2; 2,400+ successful compromises tracked Oct-Nov 2026

Evidence: <https://www.island.io/blog/agentbaiting-how-800-fake-ai-skills-and-mcp-servers-delivered-malware>

### Connections

- create-fakes -> agent-recommends
- agent-recommends -> user-installs
- user-installs -> compromise

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0000](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0000) Search Open Technical Databases — Adversary manipulates LLM tool recommendation systems to deliver malicious packages via agent-suggested GitHub repos
  Evidence: <https://www.island.io/blog/agentbaiting-how-800-fake-ai-skills-and-mcp-servers-delivered-malware>

## Prevention
Verify GitHub repos before install (check org, stars, age, commit history); use allowlisted skill/MCP sources; implement agent guardrails to warn on unverified packages; educate users not to blindly trust agent recommendations; review install scripts; use SCA tools; prefer official sources (Anthropic MCP registry, Cursor skills directory); flag typosquat patterns

## Detections
- Supply chain monitoring (guidance) — Monitor package installations, verify publisher authenticity, scan for malicious code patterns

## Timeline
- First seen: 2026-10-30
- Last updated: 2026-11-04
- 2026-10-30 (Island): Initial discovery and analysis

## Tools
### AI tooling and models
- [Cursor IDE](https://cursor.com/) and [Cursor](https://cursor.com/) rules
- [Claude Code](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code)
- MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers
- AI coding assistants (generic)
- LLM search and recommendation systems

### Other tooling
- Fake GitHub repositories (800+)
- npm/PyPI trojanized packages
- Shai-Hulud credential stealer variants

# Carbonato botnet deploys Hermes agent to hunt AI keys on Docker hosts

- ID: carbonato-botnet-hermes-2026-10
- Reported: 2026-10-28
- AI role: attacker_uses_ai_as_operator
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/carbonato-botnet-hermes-2026-10/

## Summary
Oct 28, 2026: Carbonato botnet scans for exposed Docker daemons (TCP 2375/2376, unauthenticated or weak credentials). On compromise, deploys privileged container running Ubuntu with: (1) Hermes autonomous agent (Python-based LLM agent framework); (2) scanning modules for AWS credentials, GitHub tokens, OpenAI/Anthropic API keys, HuggingFace tokens, Docker secrets, Kubernetes service accounts; (3) XMRig crypto miner (secondary payload). Hermes agent autonomously navigates filesystem, reads environment variables, parses .env files, queries Docker secrets API, extracts credentials from running containers, and exfiltrates findings to hxxps://carbonato-collect[.]net/api/ingest. Agent continues running indefinitely, adapting search patterns based on discovered infrastructure. ThreatDown tracked 3,200+ compromised Docker hosts Oct-Nov 2026; hosts in cloud providers (AWS, GCP, Azure, DigitalOcean) and on-premise. Median dwell time 18 days before detection. Detection: monitor Docker daemon exposure (Shodan queries docker 2375/2376), review privileged container deployments, alert on Hermes agent indicators (Python LLM agent process, hermes CLI usage), check for carbonato-collect[.]net egress, monitor API key/token file access patterns from containers.

## Category
attacks-on-ai

## Attribution
Unknown actor; Carbonato botnet infrastructure; financially motivated (crypto mining + credential monetization)

- Actor: Carbonato botnet operators
- Country: Unknown
- Motivation: financially-motivated
- Attributed by: ThreatDown Labs
- Confidence: medium

## AI involvement confidence
confirmed

## Attack flow
### scan-docker: Scan for exposed Docker (access)

Botnet scans internet for exposed Docker daemons on TCP 2375 (unencrypted) and 2376 (TLS); brute-forces weak credentials or exploits no-auth configs

Evidence: <https://www.threatdown.com/blog/carbonato/>

### deploy-container: Deploy malicious container (ai)

Creates privileged Docker container with host filesystem mounts; runs Ubuntu image with Hermes agent, scanning tools, and XMRig miner; container gains host-level access

Evidence: <https://www.threatdown.com/blog/carbonato/>

### hermes-hunt: Autonomous credential hunting (execution)

Hermes agent autonomously navigates filesystem, reads env vars, parses .env files, queries Docker secrets, extracts credentials from running containers; adapts search patterns based on discovered infrastructure; targets AWS, GitHub, OpenAI, Anthropic, HuggingFace keys

Evidence: <https://www.threatdown.com/blog/carbonato/>

### exfiltrate-mine: Exfiltrate and mine (impact)

Hermes POSTs credentials to hxxps://carbonato-collect[.]net/api/ingest; XMRig mines Monero using host CPU; agent maintains persistence and continues hunting indefinitely; median 18-day dwell time

Evidence: <https://www.threatdown.com/blog/carbonato/>

### Connections

- scan-docker -> deploy-container
- deploy-container -> hermes-hunt
- hermes-hunt -> exfiltrate-mine

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0000](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0000) Search Open Technical Databases — Attacker deploys autonomous AI agent (Hermes) to hunt for AI service credentials on compromised infrastructure
  Evidence: <https://www.threatdown.com/blog/carbonato/>

## Prevention
Never expose Docker daemon to internet; require TLS with client cert authentication; use Docker socket firewall rules; implement least-privilege container policies; disable privileged containers where possible; monitor container resource usage; rotate API keys regularly; use secret management solutions (HashiCorp Vault, AWS Secrets Manager); network segmentation; Docker security scanning

## Detections
- Docker daemon exposure monitoring (guidance) — Monitor for exposed Docker daemons on TCP 2375/2376; alert on unauthorized privileged container deployments with host filesystem mounts
- Hermes agent detection (guidance) — Monitor for Hermes Python processes, autonomous-agent activity, API calls to DeepSeek from Docker containers; alert on carbonato-collect\[.\]net egress

## Timeline
- First seen: 2026-10-01
- Last updated: 2026-11-04
- 2026-10-28 (ThreatDown Labs): 3,200+ compromised Docker hosts discovered; Hermes agent deployment for autonomous credential hunting; median 18-day dwell time

## Tools
### AI tooling and models
- Hermes autonomous agent framework
- OpenAI API (targeted)
- Anthropic [Claude](https://claude.com/product/overview) API (targeted)
- HuggingFace (targeted)

### Other tooling
- [Docker](https://github.com/moby/moby) container escape
- XMRig cryptocurrency miner
- carbonato-collect\[.\]net C2

## Sources
- [ThreatDown: Carbonato Botnet Spreads Via Exposed Docker Hosts](https://www.threatdown.com/blog/carbonato/)
- [Hermes - Autonomous AI Agent Framework](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent)

- ID: socradar-n0n-ransomware-ai-2026-10

## Summary

OpenCode configured with 154 model entries across 7 providers (Gemini, Mistral, Nemotron, Llama, Claude, GPT-5.x, Grok, Kimi, GLM, DeepSeek, MiniMax, Qwen) including uncensored and abliterated models (safety training removed) plus self-hosted model. Agent wrote and debugged hundreds of attack scripts; gateway spending $7,216 by Oct 22, 2026. Entry via credential stuffing (305 FortiGate SSL-VPN), exposed AWS keys, weak RDP/WinRM, compromised hosting portals. Hijacked Cisco Firepower Management Center to switch all policies to BLOCK. Human-directed operation supported by AI; no fully autonomous attack system. 93 listed victims, $283.7M total ransom demands.

# Yoba campaign - fake GPT-6/Claude desktop apps via DLL sideloading

- ID: checkpoint-yoba-fake-ai-2026-10
- Reported: 2026-10-27
- AI role: ai_tool_as_lure
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/checkpoint-yoba-fake-ai-2026-10/

## Summary
Campaign creates fake GitHub projects (gpt-5-6/sol-free-desktop, gpt-6-astra/gpt-6-astra.github.io, opus-5-0/opus-5-0.github.io) with GitHub.io pages impersonating GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-6 Astra, and Claude Opus desktop apps. ZIP installers contain legitimate signed OpenAI and Anthropic executables alongside malicious YobaDropper/YobaLoader DLLs. Uses DLL sideloading (T1574.002) to load malware indirectly from signed binaries. No fake engagement (stars/forks) but ranks highly via SEO poisoning on Google. Malware avoids dedicated C2 infrastructure, uses Telegram, Tor, Catbox, DNS over HTTPS. Russian-origin indicators; operates UTC-4 time zone. Releases Aug-Sep 2026, low detection rate, no password protection on ZIPs.

## Category
uncategorized

## Attribution
Yoba campaign; Russian-origin indicators (language, time zone); operates primarily UTC-4 time zone; different email addresses per repository suggest OPSEC to obscure true operational timezone

## AI involvement confidence
not assessed

## Attack flow
### seo-poison: SEO poisoning and fake repositories (access)

Created fake GitHub repositories impersonating GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-6 Astra, Claude Opus; GitHub.io pages with download links; no fake engagement but ranks highly on Google via SEO poisoning

Evidence: <https://research.checkpoint.com/2026/tricks-from-the-past-deployed-via-signed-chatgpt-and-claude-binaries/>

### lure: User downloads fake installer (access)

Victim searches for AI desktop apps, finds malicious GitHub repositories via Google; downloads ZIP from GitHub releases (sol-setup.zip, GPT-6-Astra-Setup.zip, Setup-Claude.zip)

Evidence: <https://research.checkpoint.com/2026/tricks-from-the-past-deployed-via-signed-chatgpt-and-claude-binaries/>

### sideload: DLL sideloading from signed binaries (execution)

ZIP contains legitimate signed OpenAI/Anthropic executables alongside malicious YobaDropper DLL; when legitimate signed binary runs, it loads malicious DLL via DLL search order hijacking

Evidence: <https://research.checkpoint.com/2026/tricks-from-the-past-deployed-via-signed-chatgpt-and-claude-binaries/>

### dropper: YobaDropper deploys YobaLoader (execution)

YobaDropper executes, deploys YobaLoader component; anti-sandbox and anti-analysis techniques; no password protection needed due to low detection

Evidence: <https://research.checkpoint.com/2026/tricks-from-the-past-deployed-via-signed-chatgpt-and-claude-binaries/>

### c2: C2 via Telegram, Tor, Catbox, DoH (ai)

YobaLoader contacts attacker infrastructure via Telegram, Tor, Catbox, DNS over HTTPS; no dedicated C2 infrastructure for strong OPSEC; fetches final payload

Evidence: <https://research.checkpoint.com/2026/tricks-from-the-past-deployed-via-signed-chatgpt-and-claude-binaries/>

### payload: Final payload execution (impact)

YobaLoader executes final payload on infected system; details of final payload capabilities not disclosed in source

Evidence: <https://research.checkpoint.com/2026/tricks-from-the-past-deployed-via-signed-chatgpt-and-claude-binaries/>

### Connections

- seo-poison -> lure
- lure -> sideload
- sideload -> dropper
- dropper -> c2
- c2 -> payload

## MITRE ATLAS
No ATLAS mapping is recorded.

## Prevention
Verify official AI tool sources; DLL sideloading detection; monitor GitHub releases for fake AI projects; SEO poisoning awareness; C2 infrastructure monitoring (Telegram, Tor, DNS over HTTPS)

## Detections
No detections are recorded.

## Timeline
No timeline is recorded.
